findings.title: No version-coordination check between the loaded standalone libduckdb and the Python duckdb wheel before pybridge hands it wheel-owned Connection* pointers
findings.description: On the macOS (and env-override) fallback path, load_duckdb() loads a SECOND copy of libduckdb to supply the C API symbols the Python wheel strips (utils.py:113-130). _find_standalone_libduckdb() returns a lib from three sources: the NUMBDUCK_LIBDUCKDB env override (utils.py:34-36), the versioned cache (utils.py:41-43), or the Homebrew/`/usr/local` paths (utils.py:23-26, 44-46). Only the download/cache path is version-pinned (the cache dir and download URL are keyed on duckdb.__version__ at utils.py:19-21,52-56). The brew paths (`/opt/homebrew/lib/libduckdb.dylib`, `/usr/local/lib/libduckdb.dylib`) and the env override are accepted with NO check that the library's version equals the installed Python `duckdb` wheel version. pybridge.extract_connection_ptr() then reads a raw `Connection*` out of the Python wheel's C++ object (pybridge.py:59-62) and passes it straight into ducklib.duckdb_query, which resolves `duckdb_query` against the standalone lib (pybridge.py:67). That pointer was constructed by the wheel's DuckDB build; the standalone lib casts it back to its own version's internal Connection class. If the two DuckDB versions differ (very plausible: `pip install duckdb==1.5.1` alongside a Homebrew duckdb at a different 1.x/1.6 release), the internal object layouts can disagree and the C API operates on a mis-typed pointer. The sibling numbox library treats this exact hazard as a bug to guard against: numbox/utils/pysqlite_bridge.py implements `libraries_coordinated()` (compares its linked sqlite version against Python's sqlite_version) and refuses to bridge a connection across mismatched copies, and numbox CLAUDE.md documents that this detect-and-refuse guard 'applies to any library'. numbduck has no equivalent guard.
findings.impact: Silent memory corruption / crashes when a user runs pybridge-based flows (registering @njit UDFs on an existing Python duckdb connection) on macOS with a Homebrew/env libduckdb whose version differs from the pip-installed duckdb wheel. No error is raised at load time; the mismatch surfaces as undefined behavior at query time. The versioned download path masks the issue in the common auto-download case, making the brew/env gap easy to miss.
findings.recommendation: Before returning a standalone/brew/env-sourced handle, verify its version matches duckdb.__version__ (e.g. call the standalone's duckdb_library_version() via ctypes and compare, or at minimum warn/refuse on mismatch), mirroring numbox's libraries_coordinated() detect-and-refuse pattern. Apply the check to the NUMBDUCK_LIBDUCKDB and brew branches, not just the version-keyed cache/download.

findings.title: pybridge Connection* extraction uses hardcoded pybind11/DuckDBPyConnection offsets validated only on duckdb 1.3.2/Linux, guarded only by an rc check that a wrong offset can bypass
findings.description: extract_connection_ptr() reads the C++ object pointer at id(conn)+16 (pybind11 instance header) and the Connection* at DuckDBPyConnection+32 (pybridge.py:59-62). The docstring states these offsets were 'Validated on duckdb 1.3.2 / Linux x86-64 / libstdc++' and 'may change with major duckdb releases.' numbduck's supported range is duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6, i.e. these fixed offsets are relied upon across 1.3.2, 1.4.x and 1.5.x wheels (and on Windows/macOS), whose bundled pybind11 version and DuckDBPyConnection C++ layout are not guaranteed to place the Connection at +32 or the holder at +16. The only safety net is the post-extraction `SELECT 1` validation (pybridge.py:64-69): it checks a return code, so it catches a wrong-but-still-valid pointer, but a version where the offset shifted yields an arbitrary/garbage pointer that can segfault inside duckdb_query before any rc is returned — an unrecoverable crash rather than the intended clean RuntimeError.
findings.impact: On a duckdb release within the supported <1.6 range (or a platform) where the wheel's C++/pybind11 layout differs from the 1.3.2/Linux baseline, extract_connection_ptr can dereference a garbage pointer and crash the process instead of raising, defeating the validation guard.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat the rc check as sufficient portability protection: gate the offsets per validated (duckdb version, platform) or derive the Connection* through a more stable path, and document/enforce which versions are actually validated rather than spanning the entire <1.6 pin on a single 1.3.2/Linux measurement.

notes: Verified against numbox _call_lib_func (numbox/core/bindings/call.py) that the SysV/AAPCS64/Win-x64 ABI split for <=16B by-value struct args (hugeint/uhugeint canonical {i64,i64}; interval {i32,i32,i64} eightbyte-repack) and by-value duckdb_result args via _call_lib_func_byval (byval pointer) are handled cross-platform, so the hugeint/uhugeint/interval migration to _call_lib_func and the fetch_chunk/result_return_type/result_statement_type byval calls are ABI-sound on Windows and Linux/ARM. duckdb_result_ty=UniTuple(intp,6) (48B deprecated duckdb_result), decimal (24B), varint/bignum (24B), blob/bit (16B) struct shapes match the stable duckdb.h layouts across 1.3-1.5 on 64-bit. The VARINT/BIGNUM enum aliasing (ducklib.py:58-62, both =35) and TIME_NS=39 (ducklib.py:66) match the understanding note's claim of a stable, appended enum; could not independently re-verify against a 1.5.x duckdb.h in this read-only environment, so not raised as a finding. find_duckdb_shared_lib's 1.3.x-in-package vs 1.4+-parent _duckdb.* split (utils.py:94-110) is anchored (regex is start-anchored so 'duckdb...' won't match '_duckdb...'); its len==1 invariant could spuriously RuntimeError on an unexpected sidecar lib but that is a robustness risk, not a demonstrable defect, and is already surfaced in loader.md. The _download_libduckdb path (no checksum/timeout, trusted without a symbol re-check) is a supply-chain/robustness concern already catalogued in the loader understanding note, not a cross-version correctness bug per se.
